bill.title: New Era of Preventing End-Stage Kidney Disease Act
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

industries.rationale: The bill establishes new training programs and centers of excellence that would operate within hospitals and health systems.
Research into rare kidney disease diagnosis, treatment, and alternatives to dialysis would directly affect medical device and pharmaceutical development in nephrology.
Health professions schools would receive funding to establish fellowship programs and expanded training curricula for kidney disease care.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create federally funded regional centers focused on rare kidney diseases, require certain medical schools to offer fellowships in rare kidney disease care for underserved populations, and expand primary care training programs to include kidney disease education. It also directs the Department of Health and Human Services to study rare kidney disease treatment, dialysis alternatives, and public awareness strategies and report findings to Congress.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys health insurance. People with an illness that is still being studied.

bill.title: To direct the President to establish an interagency task force to review, and provide recommendations on, the impact of addictive design features on youth mental health, to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish grant programs to support the activities of the task force, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

industries.rationale: The task force would examine addictive design features in digital products, which are created and deployed by technology platforms and software companies.
The bill focuses on youth mental health impacts and directs HHS to fund related activities, which may involve health providers in research or service delivery.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require the President to create a task force of federal agencies to study how design features in digital products affect young people's mental health and to recommend policy responses. The Department of Health and Human Services would award grants to support the task force's work. The bill does not itself impose new regulations on companies or change existing law governing digital platforms.

bill.title: Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act of 2026
bill.latestActionText: Received in the Senate. Read twice. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 466.
subjects: Department of Health and Human Services

industries.rationale: The bill directly funds research grants and regulatory pathways for development of drugs and therapies targeting ALS and neurodegenerative diseases.
Providers treating ALS patients may see changes in available investigational therapies and clinical trial access, though the bill focuses primarily on research and regulatory processes.

bill.plainSummary: This bill extends funding through fiscal year 2031 for federal programs that support research and development of treatments for ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease) and similar neurodegenerative diseases. It requires the National Institutes of Health to track safety data on experimental drugs and mandates that the Food and Drug Administration publish a five-year plan describing how it will help develop and approve therapies for these rare diseases. The bill also continues a public-private partnership between federal agencies and outside organizations working on neurodegenerative disease treatments.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: Washington, D.C. Admission Act
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and in addition to the Committees on Rules, Armed Services, the Judiciary, and Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
subjects: Presidents and presidential powers, Vice Presidents

industries.rationale: The bill fundamentally restructures the governance of the District, creating a new state government and redefining the federal district.
Statehood would change property tax authority and land-use regulation for most of the current District, affecting developers and property owners.
The transition of DC courts, judicial proceedings, and contractual obligations to state authority would affect legal practice and litigation in the new jurisdiction.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would admit most of the current District of Columbia as the 51st state, called Washington, Douglass Commonwealth, with two senators and one representative in Congress. A small federal district containing the Capitol, White House, Supreme Court, and nearby monuments would remain as the seat of the federal government. The bill sets up a transition process for DC laws, courts, contracts, and obligations to continue under state authority, and creates a commission to manage the shift to statehood.

bill.title: Bottles and Breastfeeding Equipment Screening Enhancement Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 161.

industries.rationale: The bill imposes new screening protocols and compliance obligations on TSA airport security operations.
Manufacturers of breast pumps, baby bottles, and related feeding equipment may face indirect effects from changed screening procedures.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Transportation Security Administration to create or update guidance for screening breast milk, baby formula, and related items at airports in ways that reduce contamination risk and follow hygiene standards. It also directs the Department of Homeland Security's inspector general to audit whether TSA is following these requirements and report the findings to Congress.

bill.title: SEED Act
bill.latestActionText: Cloture motion on the motion to proceed to the measure presented in Senate. (CR S4253)

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects early childhood education providers by changing the tax treatment of their employees' expenses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow early childhood educators (pre-kindergarten teachers and staff) to claim the same federal tax deduction for unreimbursed classroom and professional development expenses that is currently available only to kindergarten through grade 12 educators. The deduction is capped at $300 in 2025 and adjusts annually for inflation. It would reduce taxable income for eligible early childhood educators who pay out-of-pocket for supplies and training.

bill.title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 59.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new content-moderation obligations and 48-hour removal requirements on platforms that host user-generated content.
Online publishers and digital media platforms may face compliance obligations if they host user-generated intimate content.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make it a federal crime to publish intimate images or videos of someone online without their consent, including computer-generated deepfakes, when the publication is intended to cause harm or involves a minor. It would require websites and apps that host user-generated content to remove such images within 48 hours of being notified by the person depicted. Violators would face criminal penalties including prison time, fines, and mandatory restitution to victims.

plain.whoItTouches: Children, and the adults responsible for them. Anyone who uses the internet.

bill.title: GOSAFE Act
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill directly prohibits the manufacture, sale, import, and transfer of specific categories of firearms and ammunition devices.
Retailers selling firearms and ammunition would face new restrictions on what products they can legally stock and sell.
State and local governments would gain authority to use federal grant funds for buy-back programs and would enforce new criminal penalties.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit the import, sale, manufacture, transfer, and possession of gas-operated semiautomatic firearms and large-capacity ammunition magazines, with criminal penalties including fines and up to 12 months in prison for violations. Individuals possessing these firearms during a federal felony would face a mandatory minimum two-year sentence. The bill would allow state and local governments to use federal grant funds to operate buy-back programs for these firearms and magazines.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
